1765572833793740802 [2024-03-07] @christineist 💜 148 🔁 9 [(SEED) type=root]
I’m taking speech coaching from @myceliummage ! It’s 6 sessions spanning six weeks. Threading my thoughts & experience here:
├── 1765573486133801071 [2024-03-07] @sanjehorah 💜 3
│   @christineist @myceliummage looking forward to this!
├── 1765594671101977059 [2024-03-07] @christineist 💜 57 🔁 1
│   @myceliummage Okay so what I've gathered so far, I would describe the whole framework/philosophy/approach as similar to a synesthesia for emotion-language. So when you write or speak a phrase, the words and relationships between words have shape, texture, and movement. If you were to draw out
│   ↓
│   1765594983099412621 [2024-03-07] @christineist 💜 39
│   @myceliummage these shapes, it would start to make patterns and perhaps even become like a sort of pattern language. Certain types of speech, certain words, have a particular texture to them. The best example of this is when someone is speaking in a passive aggressive or manipulative way, you
│   ↓
│   1765595228277531037 [2024-03-07] @christineist 💜 42
│   @myceliummage tend to get far more interesting shapes/texture/patterns/arrows going all over the place, compared to a relatively direct sentence. By looking more carefully at the sources of chaotic patterning (edges, arrows, knots, etc), you can actually come to *see* and *uncover* emotions
│   ↓
│   1765595638123880773 [2024-03-07] @christineist 💜 35
│   @myceliummage that are hiding within them. The approach feels like it harkens a bit to Virginia Satir with her work on relational postures (see PAIRS Training Segment IV), also feels circling adjacent.
│   ↓
│   1765596028957540832 [2024-03-07] @christineist 💜 35
│   @myceliummage One big philosophical stance is to align your words to the emotions underlying them, to create a "smooth" texture. For example if you say "I'm fine" but your face is screwed up in pain, then the overall phrase has a weird texture to it because the emotion doesn't match the word.
│   ↓
│   1765597578559938586 [2024-03-07] @christineist 💜 32
│   @myceliummage People don't always talk in smooth phrases because it can be reallyyyy vulnerable to admit your own immediate emotional experience, and so you put all these confusing layers of patterning on top. Eg, "I don't know what *you* want to do, but I'm going to go to the park."
│   ↓
│   1765598087572328784 [2024-03-07] @christineist 💜 29
│   @myceliummage oh I should mention mage got to this framework from large amounts of first hand experience dealing with a lot of confusing communication, so this was like a path to un-confusing himself and finding harbor
│   ↓
│   1765598686820859945 [2024-03-07] @christineist 💜 27
│   @myceliummage There are these 3 symbols: {ϕ}{0}{1}
│   
│   In session 1 we explored {1} Negation. I wrote a piece of writing, and we went through and found all the instances of negation (not, but, un-, etc) in it. Then he had me go and rewrite the sentences without the negation, and through this
│   ↓
│   1765598931768242524 [2024-03-07] @christineist 💜 28
│   @myceliummage process I uncovered *a lot* of additional experience, emotion, and reality that was hiding in the folds. 
│   
│   For example:
│   ↓
│   1765599321213595685 [2024-03-07] @christineist 💜 38
│   1) A radiant smile that warms you and doesn’t go away like in real life but continues on, like a generous ray of sunshine visiting your bedroom for a lazy afternoon.
│   2) On earth, a radiant smile may warm you for a moment before leaving you a little hollow and blue. Here, it continues on, like a generous ray of sunshine visiting your bedroom for a lazy afternoon.
├── 1765611698075881504 [2024-03-07] @chercher_ai 💜 3
│   @christineist @myceliummage This is super great thanks for sharing 🕯️🕯️
└── 1765779673521492113 [2024-03-07] @sanjehorah 💜 2
    @christineist @myceliummage great thread. thank u for your service 🙏
